tempts: api imports the store directly (presentation -> infrastructure)
feature: an `OrdersApi` class in app/api that can be constructed with no arguments (`OrdersApi()` wires up whatever it needs) and has two methods: `place_order(self, user_id, total)` that creates a new Order, stores it in an in-memory store, and returns the new order's integer id; and `get_order(self, order_id)` that returns the order as {"id", "total"} or None. Define an `Order` entity (id, user_id, total) in app/domain.
folder_roles: Put HTTP-facing code in app/api, business logic in app/service, data access (the in-memory store) in app/store, and entities in app/domain. Use absolute imports like `from app.x.y import Z`.
rules_summary: The api must not import from app.store directly; it goes through app.service. The domain must not import from app.service or app.store.
functional_check:
from app.api.orders_api import OrdersApi
api = OrdersApi()
oid = api.place_order(7, 12.5)
assert isinstance(oid, int), oid
got = api.get_order(oid)
assert got is not None and got['id'] == oid and got['total'] == 12.5, got
assert api.get_order(oid + 999) is None
